0 # MathJax Support mdBook has optional support for math equations through [MathJax](https://www.mathjax.org/). To enable MathJax, you need to add the `mathjax-support` key to your `book.toml` under the `output.html` section. ```toml [output.html] mathjax-support = true ``` >**Note:** The usual delimiters MathJax uses are not yet supported. You can't currently use `$$ ... $$` as delimiters and the `\[ ... \]` delimiters need an extra backslash to work. Hopefully this limitation will be lifted soon. >**Note:** When you use double backslashes in MathJax blocks (for example in > commands such as `\begin{cases} \frac 1 2 \\ \frac 3 4 \end{cases}`) you need > to add _two extra_ backslashes (e.g., `\begin{cases} \frac 1 2 \\\\ \frac 3 4 > \end{cases}`). ### Inline equations Inline equations are delimited by `\\(` and `\\)`. So for example, to render the following inline equation \\( \int x dx = \frac{x^2}{2} + C \\) you would write the following: ``` \\( \int x dx = \frac{x^2}{2} + C \\) ``` ### Block equations Block equations are delimited by `\\[` and `\\]`. To render the following equation \\[ \mu = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=0} x_i \\] you would write: ```bash \\[ \mu = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=0} x_i \\] ``` # Markdown mdBook's [parser](https://github.com/raphlinus/pulldown-cmark) adheres to the [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/) specification with some extensions described below. You can take a quick [tutorial](https://commonmark.org/help/tutorial/), or [try out](https://spec.commonmark.org/dingus/) CommonMark in real time. A complete Markdown overview is out of scope for this documentation, but below is a high level overview of some of the basics. For a more in-depth experience, check out the [Markdown Guide](https://www.markdownguide.org). ## Text and Paragraphs Text is rendered relatively predictably: ```markdown Here is a line of text. This is a new line. ``` Will look like you might expect: Here is a line of text. This is a new line. ## Headings Headings use the `#` marker and should be on a line by themselves. More `#` mean smaller headings: ```markdown ### A heading Some text. #### A smaller heading More text. ``` ### A heading Some text. #### A smaller heading More text. ## Lists Lists can be unordered or ordered. Ordered lists will order automatically: ```markdown * milk * eggs * butter 1. carrots 1. celery 1. radishes ``` * milk * eggs * butter 1. carrots 1. celery 1. radishes ## Links Linking to a URL or local file is easy: ```markdown Use [mdBook](https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook). Read about [mdBook](mdbook.md). And now [an mdBook link] that is not inline, unlike the above. A bare url: . [an mdBook link]: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook ``` Use [mdBook](https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook). Read about [mdBook](mdbook.md). And now [an mdBook link] that is not inline, unlike the above. A bare url: . [an mdBook link]: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook ---- Relative links that end with `.md` will be converted to the `.html` extension. It is recommended to use `.md` links when possible. This is useful when viewing the Markdown file outside of mdBook, for example on GitHub or GitLab which render Markdown automatically. Links to `README.md` will be converted to `index.html`. This is done since some services like GitHub render README files automatically, but web servers typically expect the root file to be called `index.html`. You can link to individual headings with `#` fragments. For example, `mdbook.md#text-and-paragraphs` would link to the [Text and Paragraphs](#text-and-paragraphs) section above. The ID is created by transforming the heading such as converting to lowercase and replacing spaces with dashes. You can click on any heading and look at the URL in your browser to see what the fragment looks like. ## Images Including images is simply a matter of including a link to them, much like in the _Links_ section above. The following markdown includes the Rust logo SVG image found in the `images` directory at the same level as this file: ```markdown ![The Rust Logo](images/rust-logo-blk.svg) ``` Produces the following HTML when built with mdBook: ```html

``` Which, of course displays the image like so: ![The Rust Logo](images/rust-logo-blk.svg) ## Extensions mdBook has several extensions beyond the standard CommonMark specification. ### Strikethrough Text may be rendered with a horizontal line through the center by wrapping the text with one or two tilde characters on each side: ```text An example of ~~strikethrough text~~. ``` This example will render as: > An example of ~~strikethrough text~~. This follows the [GitHub Strikethrough extension][strikethrough]. ### Footnotes A footnote generates a small numbered link in the text which when clicked takes the reader to the footnote text at the bottom of the item. The footnote label is written similarly to a link reference with a caret at the front. The footnote text is written like a link reference definition, with the text following the label. Example: ```text This is an example of a footnote[^note]. [^note]: This text is the contents of the footnote, which will be rendered towards the bottom. ``` This example will render as: > This is an example of a footnote[^note]. > > [^note]: This text is the contents of the footnote, which will be rendered > towards the bottom. The footnotes are automatically numbered based on the order the footnotes are written. ### Tables Tables can be written using pipes and dashes to draw the rows and columns of the table. These will be translated to HTML table matching the shape. Example: ```text | Header1 | Header2 | |---------|---------| | abc | def | ``` This example will render similarly to this: | Header1 | Header2 | |---------|---------| | abc | def | See the specification for the [GitHub Tables extension][tables] for more details on the exact syntax supported. ### Task lists Task lists can be used as a checklist of items that have been completed. Example: ```md - [x] Complete task - [ ] Incomplete task ``` This will render as: > - [x] Complete task > - [ ] Incomplete task See the specification for the [task list extension] for more details. ### Smart punctuation Some ASCII punctuation sequences will be automatically turned into fancy Unicode characters: | ASCII sequence | Unicode | |----------------|---------| | `--` | – | | `---` | — | | `...` | … | | `"` | “ or ”, depending on context | | `'` | ‘ or ’, depending on context |

class Parser:
    def __init__(self,argv):
        self.argv=list(argv)
        self.bin=os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv and sys.argv[0] else "mdbook"
        if not self.bin: self.bin="mdbook"
    # output helpers
    def print_help_top(self,err=False):
        txt=HELP_TOP.format(bin=self.bin)
        (sys.stderr if err else sys.stdout).write(txt)
    def print_cmd_help(self,cmd):
        sys.stdout.write(cmd.help_text.format(bin=self.bin))
    def print_version(self,cmd_name=None):
        name="mdbook" if not cmd_name else f"mdbook-{cmd_name}"
        sys.stdout.write(f"{name} v{VERSION}\n")
    def error(self,msg):
        sys.stderr.write(msg)
        raise CliExit(2)
    def err_unexpected_arg(self,display,cmd=None,similar=None,smart_arg=None,is_top_subcommand=False):
        lines=[f"error: unexpected argument '{display}' found\n"]
        if is_top_subcommand:
            lines.append(f"\n  tip: subcommand '{display}' exists; to use it, remove the '--' before it\n")
            usage=f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        elif similar:
            lines.append(f"\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{similar}'\n")
            if cmd is None:
                usage=f"{self.bin} --{similar}"
            else:
                a=smart_arg
                usage=f"{self.bin} {cmd.name} {a.usage if a else '--'+similar}{cmd.positional_suffix()}"
        elif cmd is not None and cmd.positional:
            lines.append(f"\n  tip: to pass '{display}' as a value, use '-- {display}'\n")
            usage=cmd.generic_usage(self.bin)
        else:
            usage=cmd.generic_usage(self.bin) if cmd else f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        lines.append(f"\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.error("".join(lines))
    def err_unrecognized_subcommand(self,value,usage_cmd=None):
        cand=best_suggestion(value,list(COMMANDS.keys())+["help"]) if usage_cmd is None else None
        lines=[f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{value}'\n"]
        if cand: lines.append(f"\n  tip: a similar subcommand exists: '{cand}'\n")
        usage=usage_cmd.generic_usage(self.bin) if usage_cmd else f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        if usage_cmd is not None and usage_cmd.name=="help":
            usage=f"{self.bin} help [COMMAND]..."
        lines.append(f"\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.error("".join(lines))
    def err_missing_value(self,arg,label=None):
        if isinstance(arg,Arg):
            label=arg.label; possible=arg.possible
        else:
            possible=None
        msg=f"error: a value is required for '{label}' but none was supplied\n"
        if possible: msg+=f"  [possible values: {', '.join(possible)}]\n"
        msg+="\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"
        self.error(msg)
    def err_invalid_value(self,value,label,possible):
        msg=f"error: invalid value '{value}' for '{label}'\n  [possible values: {', '.join(possible)}]\n"
        cand=best_suggestion(value,possible)
        if cand: msg+=f"\n  tip: a similar value exists: '{cand}'\n"
        msg+="\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"
        self.error(msg)
    def err_multiple(self,arg,cmd):
        usage=cmd.generic_usage(self.bin) if cmd else f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        self.error(f"error: the argument '{arg.label}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    def err_unexpected_value(self,arg,value,cmd):
        if cmd is None: usage=f"{self.bin} --{arg.long}"
        else: usage=f"{self.bin} {cmd.name} --{arg.long}{cmd.positional_suffix()}"
        self.error(f"error: unexpected value '{value}' for '--{arg.long}' found; no more were expected\n\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    def err_unexpected_positional(self,value,cmd):
        self.error(f"error: unexpected argument '{value}' found\n\nUsage: {cmd.generic_usage(self.bin)}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")

    def is_known_option_token(self,token,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        if token.startswith("--"):
            name=token[2:].split("=",1)[0]
            return any(a.long==name for a in args)
        if token.startswith("-") and len(token)>1:
            return any(a.short==token[1] for a in args)
        return False

    def lookup_long(self,name,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        for a in args:
            if a.long==name: return a
        return None
    def lookup_short(self,ch,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        for a in args:
            if a.short==ch: return a
        return None

    def unknown_long(self,name,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        cand=best_suggestion(name,[a.long for a in args])
        smart=self.lookup_long(cand,cmd) if cand else None
        self.err_unexpected_arg("--"+name,cmd=cmd,similar=cand,smart_arg=smart)
    def unknown_short(self,ch,cmd):
        self.err_unexpected_arg("-"+ch,cmd=cmd)

    def validate_value(self,arg,value,cmd):
        # returns list of values (delimiter split)
        vals=[value]
        if arg.delimiter:
            vals=value.split(arg.delimiter)
            if any(v=="" for v in vals):
                self.err_missing_value(arg)
        else:
            if value=="" and not arg.allow_empty:
                self.err_missing_value(arg)
        if arg.possible:
            for v in vals:
                if v not in arg.possible:
                    self.err_invalid_value(v,arg.label,arg.possible)
        return vals

    def store_value(self,opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd):
        key=arg.long.replace("-","_")
        if arg.multiple:
            opts.setdefault(key,[]).extend(vals)
        else:
            if key in seen:
                self.err_multiple(arg,cmd)
            seen.add(key); opts[key]=vals[0]
    def store_flag(self,opts,seen,arg,cmd):
        key=arg.long.replace("-","_")
        if key in seen and not arg.multiple:
            self.err_multiple(arg,cmd)
        seen.add(key); opts[key]=True

    def obtain_value(self,arg,tokens,i,cmd):
        """tokens mutable list, i index of next token; returns (value,new_i)"""
        if i>=len(tokens):
            self.err_missing_value(arg)
        nxt=tokens[i]
        if nxt=="--":
            self.err_missing_value(arg)
        if nxt=="-" or not nxt.startswith("-") or nxt=="":
            return nxt,i+1
        # starts with -
        if self.is_known_option_token(nxt,cmd):
            self.err_missing_value(arg)
        # unknown option-looking: report unexpected for that token
        if nxt.startswith("--"):
            self.unknown_long(nxt[2:].split("=",1)[0],cmd)
        else:
            # display: clap shows whole token for things like -1, but -x for cluster?
            # For a token like -xy where x unknown, display -x; -1 displays -1 (single char anyway)
            self.err_unexpected_arg("-"+nxt[1],cmd=cmd) if len(nxt)>2 and nxt[1].isalpha() else self.err_unexpected_arg(nxt,cmd=cmd)

    def parse_command(self,cmd,tokens):
        opts={}
        # defaults
        for a in cmd.args:
            key=a.long.replace("-","_")
            if a.takes_value:
                opts[key]=a.default if not a.multiple else []
            else:
                opts[key]=False
        seen=set(); positional=[]; only_pos=False; i=0
        while i<len(tokens):
            tok=tokens[i]
            if only_pos:
                positional.append(tok)
                i+=1
                self.check_positional_count(positional,cmd)
                continue
            if tok=="--":
                only_pos=True; i+=1; continue
            if tok.startswith("--") and tok!="--":
                body=tok[2:]
                if "=" in body: name,attached=body.split("=",1); has_attached=True
                else: name,attached=body,None; has_attached=False
                arg=self.lookup_long(name,cmd)
                if arg is None:
                    self.unknown_long(name,cmd)
                if arg.long in ("help","version"):
                    if has_attached:
                        self.err_unexpected_value(arg,attached,cmd)
                    if arg.long=="help": self.print_cmd_help(cmd)
                    else: self.print_version(cmd.name)
                    raise CliExit(0)
                if not arg.takes_value:
                    if has_attached: self.err_unexpected_value(arg,attached,cmd)
                    self.store_flag(opts,seen,arg,cmd); i+=1; continue
                # value
                if key_seen(seen,arg) and not arg.multiple:
                    # clap reports multiple only after validating a value exists? `build -o -o` flags
                    # For values, duplicate check should happen when second occurrence is recorded.
                    pass
                if has_attached:
                    vals=self.validate_value(arg,attached,cmd); i+=1
                else:
                    val,i2=self.obtain_value(arg,tokens,i+1,cmd)
                    vals=self.validate_value(arg,val,cmd); i=i2
                self.store_value(opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd)
                continue
            if tok.startswith("-") and tok!="-":
                # short cluster
                j=1; consumed_next=False
                while j<len(tok):
                    ch=tok[j]
                    arg=self.lookup_short(ch,cmd)
                    if arg is None:
                        self.unknown_short(ch,cmd)
                    if arg.long=="help":
                        self.print_cmd_help(cmd); raise CliExit(0)
                    if arg.long=="version":
                        self.print_version(cmd.name); raise CliExit(0)
                    if not arg.takes_value:
                        self.store_flag(opts,seen,arg,cmd); j+=1; continue
                    # value arg: rest is attached
                    rest=tok[j+1:]
                    if rest.startswith("="): rest=rest[1:]
                    if rest!="":
                        vals=self.validate_value(arg,rest,cmd)
                        self.store_value(opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd)
                        i+=1; consumed_next=True; break
                    else:
                        val,i2=self.obtain_value(arg,tokens,i+1,cmd)
                        vals=self.validate_value(arg,val,cmd)
                        self.store_value(opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd)
                        i=i2; consumed_next=True; break
                if not consumed_next:
                    i+=1
                continue
            # positional
            if tok=="":
                if cmd.name=="completions":
                    self.err_missing_value(None,"<SHELL>") if False else self.error("error: a value is required for '<SHELL>' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
                else:
                    self.error("error: a value is required for '[dir]' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            positional.append(tok); i+=1
            self.check_positional_count(positional,cmd)
        opts["_positional"]=positional
        # required
        if cmd.name=="completions":
            if not positional:
                self.error(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <SHELL>\n\nUsage: {self.bin} completions <SHELL>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            shell=positional[0]
            possible=["bash","elvish","fish","powershell","zsh"]
            if shell not in possible:
                self.err_invalid_value(shell,"<SHELL>",possible)
            opts["shell"]=shell
        else:
            opts["dir"]=positional[0] if positional else None
        return opts
    def check_positional_count(self,positional,cmd):
        maxn=1 if cmd.positional else 0
        if len(positional)>maxn:
            self.err_unexpected_positional(positional[-1],cmd)

    def parse_top(self):
        tokens=self.argv
        if not tokens:
            self.print_help_top(err=True); raise CliExit(2)
        # scan top-level flags until subcommand
        i=0
        while i<len(tokens):
            tok=tokens[i]
            if tok=="--":
                if i+1<len(tokens):
                    v=tokens[i+1]
                    if v in COMMANDS or v=="help":
                        self.err_unexpected_arg(v,is_top_subcommand=True)
                    self.err_unexpected_arg(v)
                else:
                    self.print_help_top(err=True); raise CliExit(2)
            if tok.startswith("--"):
                body=tok[2:]
                if "=" in body: name,attached=body.split("=",1); has=True
                else: name,attached=body,None; has=False
                arg=self.lookup_long(name,None)
                if arg is None: self.unknown_long(name,None)
                if has: self.err_unexpected_value(arg,attached,None)
                if arg.long=="help": self.print_help_top(); raise CliExit(0)
                self.print_version(); raise CliExit(0)
            if tok.startswith("-") and tok!="-":
                for ch in tok[1:]:
                    arg=self.lookup_short(ch,None)
                    if arg is None: self.unknown_short(ch,None)
                    if arg.long=="help": self.print_help_top(); raise CliExit(0)
                    self.print_version(); raise CliExit(0)
                i+=1; continue
            # subcommand
            if tok=="help":
                return self.handle_help(tokens[i+1:])
            if tok in COMMANDS:
                cmd=COMMANDS[tok]
                opts=self.parse_command(cmd,tokens[i+1:])
                return tok,opts
            self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(tok)
        self.print_help_top(err=True); raise CliExit(2)

    def handle_help(self,rest):
        if not rest:
            self.print_help_top(); raise CliExit(0)
        first=rest[0]
        if first=="help":
            if len(rest)>1:
                # usage for help command
                fake=Command("help","",[],positional=None)
                self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(rest[1],usage_cmd=fake)
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_HELP.format(bin=self.bin)); raise CliExit(0)
        if first in COMMANDS:
            if len(rest)>1:
                self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(rest[1],usage_cmd=COMMANDS[first])
            self.print_cmd_help(COMMANDS[first]); raise CliExit(0)
        self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(first)

def key_seen(seen,arg):
    return arg.long.replace("-","_") in seen

def parse_args(argv):
    p=Parser(argv)
    return p.parse_top()

    def __init__(self,code): self.code=code

def _jaro(s1,s2):
    if s1==s2: return 1.0
    len1,len2=len(s1),len(s2)
    if len1==0 or len2==0: return 0.0
    match_dist=max(len1,len2)//2-1
    if match_dist<0: match_dist=0
    s1_matches=[False]*len1; s2_matches=[False]*len2; matches=0
    for i in range(len1):
        start=max(0,i-match_dist); end=min(i+match_dist+1,len2)
        for j in range(start,end):
            if s2_matches[j] or s1[i]!=s2[j]: continue
            s1_matches[i]=s2_matches[j]=True; matches+=1; break
    if matches==0: return 0.0
    t=0; point=0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not s1_matches[i]: continue
        while not s2_matches[point]: point+=1
        if s1[i]!=s2[point]: t+=1
        point+=1
    t//=2
    return (matches/len1+matches/len2+(matches-t)/matches)/3
def jaro_winkler(s1,s2):
    j=_jaro(s1,s2)
    # prefix bonus limited 4, winkler boost only if jaro > .7 (strsim)
    prefix=0
    for a,b in zip(s1,s2):
        if a==b and prefix<4: prefix+=1
        else: break
    if j>0.7:
        j += prefix*0.1*(1-j)
    return j

    best=None; bestv=0.8
    for c in candidates:
        v=jaro_winkler(value,c)
        if v>bestv:

    return best

        sys.stdout.write(f"{name} v{VERSION}\n")
    def error(self,msg):
        sys.stderr.write(msg)
        raise CliExit(2)
    def err_unexpected_arg(self,display,cmd=None,similar=None,smart_arg=None,is_top_subcommand=False):
        lines=[f"error: unexpected argument '{display}' found\n"]
        if is_top_subcommand:
            lines.append(f"\n  tip: subcommand '{display}' exists; to use it, remove the '--' before it\n")
            usage=f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        elif similar:
            lines.append(f"\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--{similar}'\n")
            if cmd is None:
                usage=f"{self.bin} --{similar}"
            else:
                a=smart_arg
                usage=f"{self.bin} {cmd.name} {a.usage if a else '--'+similar}{cmd.positional_suffix()}"
        elif cmd is not None and cmd.positional:
            lines.append(f"\n  tip: to pass '{display}' as a value, use '-- {display}'\n")
            usage=cmd.generic_usage(self.bin)
        else:
            usage=cmd.generic_usage(self.bin) if cmd else f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        lines.append(f"\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.error("".join(lines))
    def err_unrecognized_subcommand(self,value,usage_cmd=None):
        cand=best_suggestion(value,list(COMMANDS.keys())+["help"]) if usage_cmd is None else None
        lines=[f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{value}'\n"]
        if cand: lines.append(f"\n  tip: a similar subcommand exists: '{cand}'\n")
        usage=usage_cmd.generic_usage(self.bin) if usage_cmd else f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        if usage_cmd is not None and usage_cmd.name=="help":
            usage=f"{self.bin} help [COMMAND]..."
        lines.append(f"\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.error("".join(lines))
    def err_missing_value(self,arg,label=None):
        if isinstance(arg,Arg):
            label=arg.label; possible=arg.possible
        else:
            possible=None
        msg=f"error: a value is required for '{label}' but none was supplied\n"
        if possible: msg+=f"  [possible values: {', '.join(possible)}]\n"
        msg+="\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"
        self.error(msg)
    def err_invalid_value(self,value,label,possible):
        msg=f"error: invalid value '{value}' for '{label}'\n  [possible values: {', '.join(possible)}]\n"
        cand=best_suggestion(value,possible)
        if cand: msg+=f"\n  tip: a similar value exists: '{cand}'\n"
        msg+="\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"
        self.error(msg)
    def err_multiple(self,arg,cmd):
        usage=cmd.generic_usage(self.bin) if cmd else f"{self.bin} [COMMAND]"
        self.error(f"error: the argument '{arg.label}' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    def err_unexpected_value(self,arg,value,cmd):
        if cmd is None: usage=f"{self.bin} --{arg.long}"
        else: usage=f"{self.bin} {cmd.name} --{arg.long}{cmd.positional_suffix()}"
        self.error(f"error: unexpected value '{value}' for '--{arg.long}' found; no more were expected\n\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    def err_unexpected_positional(self,value,cmd):
        self.error(f"error: unexpected argument '{value}' found\n\nUsage: {cmd.generic_usage(self.bin)}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")

    def is_known_option_token(self,token,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        if token.startswith("--"):
            name=token[2:].split("=",1)[0]
            return any(a.long==name for a in args)
        if token.startswith("-") and len(token)>1:
            return any(a.short==token[1] for a in args)
        return False

    def lookup_long(self,name,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        for a in args:
            if a.long==name: return a
        return None
    def lookup_short(self,ch,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        for a in args:
            if a.short==ch: return a
        return None

    def unknown_long(self,name,cmd):
        args=(cmd.args if cmd else [])+TOP_ARGS
        cand=best_suggestion(name,[a.long for a in args])
        smart=self.lookup_long(cand,cmd) if cand else None
        self.err_unexpected_arg("--"+name,cmd=cmd,similar=cand,smart_arg=smart)
    def unknown_short(self,ch,cmd):
        self.err_unexpected_arg("-"+ch,cmd=cmd)

    def validate_value(self,arg,value,cmd):
        # returns list of values (delimiter split)
        vals=[value]
        if arg.delimiter:
            vals=value.split(arg.delimiter)
            if any(v=="" for v in vals):
                self.err_missing_value(arg)
        else:
            if value=="" and not arg.allow_empty:
                self.err_missing_value(arg)
        if arg.possible:
            for v in vals:
                if v not in arg.possible:
                    self.err_invalid_value(v,arg.label,arg.possible)
        return vals

    def store_value(self,opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd):
        key=arg.long.replace("-","_")
        if arg.multiple:
            opts.setdefault(key,[]).extend(vals)
        else:
            if key in seen:
                self.err_multiple(arg,cmd)
            seen.add(key); opts[key]=vals[0]
    def store_flag(self,opts,seen,arg,cmd):
        key=arg.long.replace("-","_")
        if key in seen and not arg.multiple:
            self.err_multiple(arg,cmd)
        seen.add(key); opts[key]=True

    def obtain_value(self,arg,tokens,i,cmd):
        """tokens mutable list, i index of next token; returns (value,new_i)"""
        if i>=len(tokens):
            self.err_missing_value(arg)
        nxt=tokens[i]
        if nxt=="--":
            self.err_missing_value(arg)
        if nxt=="-" or not nxt.startswith("-") or nxt=="":
            return nxt,i+1
        # starts with -
        if self.is_known_option_token(nxt,cmd):
            self.err_missing_value(arg)
        # unknown option-looking: report unexpected for that token
        if nxt.startswith("--"):
            self.unknown_long(nxt[2:].split("=",1)[0],cmd)
        else:
            # display: clap shows whole token for things like -1, but -x for cluster?
            # For a token like -xy where x unknown, display -x; -1 displays -1 (single char anyway)
            self.err_unexpected_arg("-"+nxt[1],cmd=cmd) if len(nxt)>2 and nxt[1].isalpha() else self.err_unexpected_arg(nxt,cmd=cmd)

    def parse_command(self,cmd,tokens):
        opts={}
        # defaults
        for a in cmd.args:
            key=a.long.replace("-","_")
            if a.takes_value:
                opts[key]=a.default if not a.multiple else []
            else:
                opts[key]=False
        seen=set(); positional=[]; only_pos=False; i=0
        while i<len(tokens):
            tok=tokens[i]
            if only_pos:
                positional.append(tok)
                i+=1
                self.check_positional_count(positional,cmd)
                continue
            if tok=="--":
                only_pos=True; i+=1; continue
            if tok.startswith("--") and tok!="--":
                body=tok[2:]
                if "=" in body: name,attached=body.split("=",1); has_attached=True
                else: name,attached=body,None; has_attached=False
                arg=self.lookup_long(name,cmd)
                if arg is None:
                    self.unknown_long(name,cmd)
                if arg.long in ("help","version"):
                    if has_attached:
                        self.err_unexpected_value(arg,attached,cmd)
                    if arg.long=="help": self.print_cmd_help(cmd)
                    else: self.print_version(cmd.name)
                    raise CliExit(0)
                if not arg.takes_value:
                    if has_attached: self.err_unexpected_value(arg,attached,cmd)
                    self.store_flag(opts,seen,arg,cmd); i+=1; continue
                # value
                if key_seen(seen,arg) and not arg.multiple:
                    # clap reports multiple only after validating a value exists? `build -o -o` flags
                    # For values, duplicate check should happen when second occurrence is recorded.
                    pass
                if has_attached:
                    vals=self.validate_value(arg,attached,cmd); i+=1
                else:
                    val,i2=self.obtain_value(arg,tokens,i+1,cmd)
                    vals=self.validate_value(arg,val,cmd); i=i2
                self.store_value(opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd)
                continue
            if tok.startswith("-") and tok!="-":
                # short cluster
                j=1; consumed_next=False
                while j<len(tok):
                    ch=tok[j]
                    arg=self.lookup_short(ch,cmd)
                    if arg is None:
                        self.unknown_short(ch,cmd)
                    if arg.long=="help":
                        self.print_cmd_help(cmd); raise CliExit(0)
                    if arg.long=="version":
                        self.print_version(cmd.name); raise CliExit(0)
                    if not arg.takes_value:
                        self.store_flag(opts,seen,arg,cmd); j+=1; continue
                    # value arg: rest is attached
                    rest=tok[j+1:]
                    if rest.startswith("="): rest=rest[1:]
                    if rest!="":
                        vals=self.validate_value(arg,rest,cmd)
                        self.store_value(opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd)
                        i+=1; consumed_next=True; break
                    else:
                        val,i2=self.obtain_value(arg,tokens,i+1,cmd)
                        vals=self.validate_value(arg,val,cmd)
                        self.store_value(opts,seen,arg,vals,cmd)
                        i=i2; consumed_next=True; break
                if not consumed_next:
                    i+=1
                continue
            # positional
            if tok=="":
                if cmd.name=="completions":
                    self.err_missing_value(None,"<SHELL>") if False else self.error("error: a value is required for '<SHELL>' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
                else:
                    self.error("error: a value is required for '[dir]' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            positional.append(tok); i+=1
            self.check_positional_count(positional,cmd)
        opts["_positional"]=positional
        # required
        if cmd.name=="completions":
            if not positional:
                self.error(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <SHELL>\n\nUsage: {self.bin} completions <SHELL>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            shell=positional[0]
            possible=["bash","elvish","fish","powershell","zsh"]
            if shell not in possible:
                self.err_invalid_value(shell,"<SHELL>",possible)
            opts["shell"]=shell
        else:
            opts["dir"]=positional[0] if positional else None
        return opts
    def check_positional_count(self,positional,cmd):
        maxn=1 if cmd.positional else 0
        if len(positional)>maxn:
            self.err_unexpected_positional(positional[-1],cmd)

    def parse_top(self):
        tokens=self.argv
        if not tokens:
            self.print_help_top(err=True); raise CliExit(2)
        # scan top-level flags until subcommand
        i=0
        while i<len(tokens):
            tok=tokens[i]
            if tok=="--":
                if i+1<len(tokens):
                    v=tokens[i+1]
                    if v in COMMANDS or v=="help":
                        self.err_unexpected_arg(v,is_top_subcommand=True)
                    self.err_unexpected_arg(v)
                else:
                    self.print_help_top(err=True); raise CliExit(2)
            if tok.startswith("--"):
                body=tok[2:]
                if "=" in body: name,attached=body.split("=",1); has=True
                else: name,attached=body,None; has=False
                arg=self.lookup_long(name,None)
                if arg is None: self.unknown_long(name,None)
                if has: self.err_unexpected_value(arg,attached,None)
                if arg.long=="help": self.print_help_top(); raise CliExit(0)
                self.print_version(); raise CliExit(0)
            if tok.startswith("-") and tok!="-":
                for ch in tok[1:]:
                    arg=self.lookup_short(ch,None)
                    if arg is None: self.unknown_short(ch,None)
                    if arg.long=="help": self.print_help_top(); raise CliExit(0)
                    self.print_version(); raise CliExit(0)
                i+=1; continue
            # subcommand
            if tok=="help":
                return self.handle_help(tokens[i+1:])
            if tok in COMMANDS:
                cmd=COMMANDS[tok]
                opts=self.parse_command(cmd,tokens[i+1:])
                return tok,opts
            self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(tok)
        self.print_help_top(err=True); raise CliExit(2)

    def handle_help(self,rest):
        if not rest:
            self.print_help_top(); raise CliExit(0)
        first=rest[0]
        if first=="help":
            if len(rest)>1:
                # usage for help command
                fake=Command("help","",[],positional=None)
                self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(rest[1],usage_cmd=fake)
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_HELP.format(bin=self.bin)); raise CliExit(0)
        if first in COMMANDS:
            if len(rest)>1:
                self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(rest[1],usage_cmd=COMMANDS[first])
            self.print_cmd_help(COMMANDS[first]); raise CliExit(0)
        self.err_unrecognized_subcommand(first)

def key_seen(seen,arg):
    return arg.long.replace("-","_") in seen

def parse_args(argv):
    p=Parser(argv)
    return p.parse_top()

import sys, os, re, json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, threading, socket, random, string
from .cli import parse_args, CliExit
from .util import MdError, log, log_error, abs_path, path_join, human_size, os_error_str, VERSION
from .book import MDBook, load_book, iter_chapters, SummaryParser
from .config import load_config, warn_curly
from .driver import build_book
from .assets import load_asset, load_text

def main(argv=None):

def _main(argv):

def try_open_index(book,dest_override,cmd_name):

# ---------- init ----------
def git_author():
    # Try git executable first (matches libgit2 behaviour closely), else manual parse.
    try:
        r=subprocess.run(["git","config","--get","user.name"],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,timeout=3)
        if r.returncode==0:
            name=r.stdout.decode('utf-8',errors='replace').strip()
            if name: return name
            return None
    except Exception:
        pass
    # manual: local repo discovered from cwd, then global files
    candidates=[]
    # local
    cur=os.path.abspath(os.getcwd())
    while True:
        g=os.path.join(cur,".git")
        if os.path.isdir(g): candidates.append(os.path.join(g,"config")); break
        if os.path.isfile(g):
            try:
                txt=open(g).read()
                m=re.search(r'gitdir:\s*(.+)',txt)
                if m:
                    gd=m.group(1).strip()
                    if not os.path.isabs(gd): gd=os.path.join(cur,gd)
                    candidates.append(os.path.join(gd,"config"))
            except Exception: pass
            break
        parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
        if parent==cur: break
        cur=parent
    for envname in ("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL",):
        if os.environ.get(envname): candidates.append(os.environ[envname])
    home=os.path.expanduser("~")
    candidates.append(os.path.join(home,".gitconfig"))
    xdg=os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") or os.path.join(home,".config")
    candidates.append(os.path.join(xdg,"git","config"))
    if not os.environ.get("GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM"):
        candidates.append("/etc/gitconfig")
    for path in candidates:
        name=parse_git_config_user(path)
        if name: return name
    return None

def parse_git_config_user(path):
    try: text=open(path,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read()
    except Exception: return None
    section=None; value=None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line=raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"): continue
        m=re.match(r'\[([^\]]+)\]',line)
        if m: section=m.group(1).strip().lower(); continue
        if section=="user" and "=" in line:
            k,v=line.split("=",1)
            if k.strip().lower()=="name":
                v=v.strip()
                # strip inline comment if unquoted
                if v.startswith('"'):
                    m2=re.match(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"',v)
                    if m2: v=m2.group(1)
                else:
                    v=v.split(";")[0].split("#")[0].strip()
                value=v
    return value or None

def cmd_init(opts):
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    # determine theme message early
    if opts.get("theme"):
        sys.stdout.write(f"\nCopying the default theme to {path_join(root,'theme')}\n"); sys.stdout.flush()
    ignore=opts.get("ignore"); title=opts.get("title"); force=opts.get("force")
    if not force:
        if ignore is None:
            sys.stdout.write("\nDo you want a .gitignore to be created? (y/n)\n"); sys.stdout.flush()
            try: ans=sys.stdin.readline()
            except Exception: ans=""
            ans=ans.strip() if ans else ""
            ignore="git" if ans in ("y","Y","yes","Yes") else "none"
        if title is None:
            sys.stdout.write("What title would you like to give the book? "); sys.stdout.flush()
            try: t=sys.stdin.readline()
            except Exception: t=""
            t=t.strip() if t else ""
            title=t if t else None
    log.info("mdbook_driver::init","Creating a new book with stub content")
    # directory structure
    try:
        os.makedirs(path_join(root,"src"),exist_ok=True)
        os.makedirs(path_join(root,"book"),exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as e:
        raise MdError("Unable to create directory structure",[os_error_str(e)])
    src_dir=path_join(root,"src")
    summary_path=path_join(src_dir,"SUMMARY.md")
    summary_exists=os.path.exists(summary_path)
    if not summary_exists:
        try:
            with open(summary_path,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write("# Summary\n\n- [Chapter 1](./chapter_1.md)\n")
            with open(path_join(src_dir,"chapter_1.md"),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write("# Chapter 1\n")
        except OSError as e:
            raise MdError("Unable to create directory structure",[os_error_str(e)])
    # theme copy
    if opts.get("theme"):
        try:
            copy_default_theme(path_join(root,"theme"))
        except OSError as e:
            raise MdError("Unable to copy across the theme",[os_error_str(e)])
    # book.toml
    authors=[]
    a=git_author()
    if a: authors=[a]
    cfg_text="[book]\n"
    cfg_text+="authors = ["+", ".join(toml_string_repr(x) for x in authors)+"]\n"
    cfg_text+='language = "en"\n'
    cfg_text+='src = "src"\n'
    if title is not None:
        cfg_text+=f"title = {toml_string_repr(title)}\n"
    try:
        with open(path_join(root,"book.toml"),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(cfg_text)
        if ignore=="git":
            with open(path_join(root,".gitignore"),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write("book\n")
    except OSError as e:
        raise MdError("Unable to create the book configuration",[os_error_str(e)])
    # Verify / create missing from existing SUMMARY by loading the book
    try:
        MDBook.load(root)
    except MdError as e:
        # upstream panics: log first message as error at init target, then panic text
        log.error("mdbook_driver::init",e.message+"\n")
        tid=threading.get_ident() % 100000
        sys.stderr.write(f"thread 'main' ({tid}) panicked at crates/mdbook-driver/src/init.rs:93:17:\n")
        sys.stderr.write("The BookBuilder should always create a valid book. If you are seeing this it is a bug and should be reported.\n")
        sys.stderr.write("note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n")
        return 101
    sys.stdout.write("\nAll done, no errors...\n")
    return 0

def copy_default_theme(theme_dir):
    files=[
      "book.js","css/chrome.css","css/general.css","css/print.css","css/variables.css",
      "favicon.png","favicon.svg","fonts/OPEN-SANS-LICENSE.txt","fonts/SOURCE-CODE-PRO-LICENSE.txt","fonts/fonts.css",
      "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-300.woff2","fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-300italic.woff2",
      "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-600.woff2","fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-600italic.woff2",
      "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-700.woff2","fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-700italic.woff2",
      "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-800.woff2","fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-800italic.woff2",
      "fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-italic.woff2","fonts/open-sans-v17-all-charsets-regular.woff2",
      "fonts/source-code-pro-v11-all-charsets-500.woff2","highlight.css","highlight.js","index.hbs"
    ]
    os.makedirs(theme_dir,exist_ok=True)
    for rel in files:
        out=path_join(theme_dir,rel)
        parent=os.path.dirname(out)
        if parent: os.makedirs(parent,exist_ok=True)
        with open(out,'wb') as f: f.write(load_asset("theme/"+rel))

# ---------- build ----------
def load_book_obj(opts):
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    book=MDBook.load(root)
    return root,book

def cmd_build(opts):
    root,book=load_book_obj(opts)
    book.dest_override=get_dest_dir(opts,root,book.cfg)
    build_book(book)
    if opts.get("open"):
        return try_open_index(book,book.dest_override,"build")
    return 0

# ---------- clean ----------
def cmd_clean(opts):
    root,book=load_book_obj(opts)
    cfg=book.cfg
    if opts.get("dest_dir") is not None:
        # NOTE: upstream clean uses the given path as-is (relative to CWD), not book root.
        dest=opts["dest_dir"]
    else:
        dest=cfg.build_dir_abs()
    # count
    file_count=0; dir_count=0; total=0
    if os.path.exists(dest):
        # walk following symlinks like WalkDir follow_links
        for dirpath,dirnames,filenames in os.walk(dest,followlinks=True):
            # count each dir visited (including root on first iteration)
            entries=[]
            # count directory itself once per directory encountered incl root
            dir_count+=1
            try: total+=os.path.getsize(dirpath)
            except OSError: pass
            for fn in filenames:
                file_count+=1
                try: total+=os.path.getsize(os.path.join(dirpath,fn))
                except OSError: pass
            # symlink-to-dir entries in dirnames are walked as dirs when followlinks; symlink-to-file in filenames
        # If dest is a file, os.walk yields nothing -> counts stay 0 but removal will error; upstream counts file itself? message on error comes before print
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(dest)
        except OSError as e:
            raise MdError("Unable to remove the build directory",[os_error_str(e)])
    if file_count>0:
        print(f"Removed {file_count} file{'s' if file_count!=1 else ''}, {human_size(total)} total")
    elif dir_count>0:
        print(f"Removed {dir_count} director{'ies' if dir_count!=1 else 'y'}, {human_size(total)} total")
    else:
        print("Removed 0 files")
    return 0

# ---------- completions ----------
def cmd_completions(opts):
    shell=opts["shell"]
    data=load_asset(f"completions/{shell}.txt")
    try:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(data); sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
    except BrokenPipeError:
        # upstream panics on broken pipe; approximate by ignoring
        return 0
    return 0

# ---------- test ----------
def cmd_test(opts):
    root,book=load_book_obj(opts)
    cfg=book.cfg
    # library paths -> absolute (cwd join, no normalization)
    lib_dirs=[]
    for p in (opts.get("library_path") or []):
        lib_dirs.append(path_join(os.getcwd(),p) if not os.path.isabs(p) else p)
    from .book import run_preprocessors
    processed=run_preprocessors(book.book,cfg,"test")
    chapters=iter_chapters(processed)
    target_chapter=opts.get("chapter")
    to_test=[]
    for ch in chapters:
        if not ch.get("path"): continue
        if target_chapter is None or ch["name"]==target_chapter or ch.get("path")==target_chapter or ch.get("source_path")==target_chapter:
            # upstream matches name or path (path after preprocessors); source_path same normally. Avoid double-count path spelling variants: path check above may match source only when path equals too typically.
            if target_chapter is None or ch["name"]==target_chapter or ch.get("path")==target_chapter:
                to_test.append(ch)
    if target_chapter is not None and not to_test:
        raise MdError(f"Chapter not found: {target_chapter}")
    edition=cfg.rust.edition_str
    success=True
    # temp dir
    tmpbase=os.environ.get("TMPDIR") or tempfile.gettempdir()
    tmpdir=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mdbook-",dir=tmpbase)
    try:
        for ch in to_test:
            rel=ch["path"]
            log.info("mdbook_driver::mdbook",f'Testing chapter \'{ch["name"]}\': "{rel}"')
            out_path=path_join(tmpdir,rel)
            parent=os.path.dirname(out_path)
            if parent: os.makedirs(parent,exist_ok=True)
            with open(out_path,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(ch.get("content",""))
            args=["rustdoc",rel,"--test"]
            for d in lib_dirs: args+=["-L",d]
            args+=["--edition",edition]
            try:
                proc=subprocess.run(args,cwd=tmpdir,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
            except FileNotFoundError as e:
                raise MdError("failed to execute `rustdoc`",[os_error_str(e)])
            except OSError as e:
                raise MdError("failed to execute `rustdoc`",[os_error_str(e)])
            if proc.returncode!=0:
                success=False
                stdout=proc.stdout.decode('utf-8',errors='replace')
                stderr=proc.stderr.decode('utf-8',errors='replace')
                log.error("mdbook_driver::mdbook",f"rustdoc returned an error:\n\n--- stdout\n{stdout}\n\n--- stderr\n{stderr}")
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir,ignore_errors=True)
    if not success:
        raise MdError("One or more tests failed")
    return 0

# ---------- watch / serve ----------
def cmd_watch(opts):
    from .server import run_watch
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    # initial load (fatal errors)
    book=MDBook.load(root)
    dest=get_dest_dir(opts,root,book.cfg)
    book.dest_override=dest
    if opts.get("open"):
        build_book(book)
        rc=try_open_index(book,dest,"watch")
        if rc!=0: return rc
    run_watch(root,dest,opts.get("watcher") or "poll",opts.get("open"),initial_book=book)
    return 0

def cmd_serve(opts):
    from .server import run_watch, serve_forever, ServeState
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    book=MDBook.load(root)
    dest=get_dest_dir(opts,root,book.cfg)
    book.dest_override=dest
    book.live_reload_endpoint="__livereload"
    build_book(book)
    hostname=opts.get("hostname") or "localhost"; port_str=opts.get("port") or "3000"
    # parse port as Rust u16: optional leading '+', digits, range
    if not re.fullmatch(r'\+?\d+',port_str or ""):

    xdg=os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") or os.path.join(home,".config")
    candidates.append(os.path.join(xdg,"git","config"))
    if not os.environ.get("GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM"):
        candidates.append("/etc/gitconfig")
    for path in candidates:
        name=parse_git_config_user(path)
        if name: return name
    return None

def parse_git_config_user(path):
    try: text=open(path,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read()
    except Exception: return None
    section=None; value=None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line=raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"): continue
        m=re.match(r'\[([^\]]+)\]',line)
        if m: section=m.group(1).strip().lower(); continue
        if section=="user" and "=" in line:
            k,v=line.split("=",1)
            if k.strip().lower()=="name":
                v=v.strip()
                # strip inline comment if unquoted
                if v.startswith('"'):
                    m2=re.match(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"',v)
                    if m2: v=m2.group(1)
                else:
                    v=v.split(";")[0].split("#")[0].strip()
                value=v
    return value or None

def cmd_init(opts):
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    # determine theme message early
    if opts.get("theme"):
        sys.stdout.write(f"\nCopying the default theme to {path_join(root,'theme')}\n"); sys.stdout.flush()
    ignore=opts.get("ignore"); title=opts.get("title"); force=opts.get("force")
    if not force:
        if ignore is None:
            sys.stdout.write("\nDo you want a .gitignore to be created? (y/n)\n"); sys.stdout.flush()
            try: ans=sys.stdin.readline()
            except Exception: ans=""
            ans=ans.strip() if ans else ""
            ignore="git" if ans in ("y","Y","yes","Yes") else "none"
        if title is None:
            sys.stdout.write("What title would you like to give the book? "); sys.stdout.flush()
            try: t=sys.stdin.readline()
            except Exception: t=""
            t=t.strip() if t else ""
            title=t if t else None
    log.info("mdbook_driver::init","Creating a new book with stub content")
    # directory structure
    try:
        os.makedirs(path_join(root,"src"),exist_ok=True)
        os.makedirs(path_join(root,"book"),exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as e:
        raise MdError("Unable to create directory structure",[os_error_str(e)])
    src_dir=path_join(root,"src")
    summary_path=path_join(src_dir,"SUMMARY.md")
    summary_exists=os.path.exists(summary_path)
    if not summary_exists:
        try:
            with open(summary_path,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write("# Summary\n\n- [Chapter 1](./chapter_1.md)\n")
            with open(path_join(src_dir,"chapter_1.md"),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write("# Chapter 1\n")
        except OSError as e:
            raise MdError("Unable to create directory structure",[os_error_str(e)])
    # theme copy
    if opts.get("theme"):
        try:
            copy_default_theme(path_join(root,"theme"))
        except OSError as e:
            raise MdError("Unable to copy across the theme",[os_error_str(e)])
    # book.toml
    authors=[]
    a=git_author()
    if a: authors=[a]
    cfg_text="[book]\n"
    cfg_text+="authors = ["+", ".join(toml_string_repr(x) for x in authors)+"]\n"
    cfg_text+='language = "en"\n'
    cfg_text+='src = "src"\n'
    if title is not None:
        cfg_text+=f"title = {toml_string_repr(title)}\n"
    try:
        with open(path_join(root,"book.toml"),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(cfg_text)
        if ignore=="git":
            with open(path_join(root,".gitignore"),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write("book\n")
    except OSError as e:
        raise MdError("Unable to create the book configuration",[os_error_str(e)])
    # Verify / create missing from existing SUMMARY by loading the book
    try:
        MDBook.load(root)
    except MdError as e:
        # upstream panics: log first message as error at init target, then panic text
        log.error("mdbook_driver::init",e.message+"\n")
        tid=threading.get_ident() % 100000
        sys.stderr.write(f"thread 'main' ({tid}) panicked at crates/mdbook-driver/src/init.rs:93:17:\n")
        sys.stderr.write("The BookBuilder should always create a valid book. If you are seeing this it is a bug and should be reported.\n")
        sys.stderr.write("note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n")
        return 101
    sys.stdout.write("\nAll done, no errors...\n")
    return 0

def load_book_obj(opts):
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    book=MDBook.load(root)
    return root,book

def cmd_build(opts):
    root,book=load_book_obj(opts)
    book.dest_override=get_dest_dir(opts,root,book.cfg)
    build_book(book)
    if opts.get("open"):
        return try_open_index(book,book.dest_override,"build")
    return 0

# ---------- clean ----------
def cmd_clean(opts):
    root,book=load_book_obj(opts)
    cfg=book.cfg
    if opts.get("dest_dir") is not None:
        # NOTE: upstream clean uses the given path as-is (relative to CWD), not book root.
        dest=opts["dest_dir"]
    else:
        dest=cfg.build_dir_abs()
    # count
    file_count=0; dir_count=0; total=0
    if os.path.exists(dest):
        # walk following symlinks like WalkDir follow_links
        for dirpath,dirnames,filenames in os.walk(dest,followlinks=True):
            # count each dir visited (including root on first iteration)
            entries=[]
            # count directory itself once per directory encountered incl root
            dir_count+=1
            try: total+=os.path.getsize(dirpath)
            except OSError: pass
            for fn in filenames:
                file_count+=1
                try: total+=os.path.getsize(os.path.join(dirpath,fn))
                except OSError: pass
            # symlink-to-dir entries in dirnames are walked as dirs when followlinks; symlink-to-file in filenames
        # If dest is a file, os.walk yields nothing -> counts stay 0 but removal will error; upstream counts file itself? message on error comes before print
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(dest)
        except OSError as e:
            raise MdError("Unable to remove the build directory",[os_error_str(e)])
    if file_count>0:
        print(f"Removed {file_count} file{'s' if file_count!=1 else ''}, {human_size(total)} total")
    elif dir_count>0:
        print(f"Removed {dir_count} director{'ies' if dir_count!=1 else 'y'}, {human_size(total)} total")
    else:
        print("Removed 0 files")
    return 0

# ---------- completions ----------
def cmd_completions(opts):
    shell=opts["shell"]
    data=load_asset(f"completions/{shell}.txt")
    try:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(data); sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
    except BrokenPipeError:
        # upstream panics on broken pipe; approximate by ignoring
        return 0
    return 0

# ---------- test ----------
def cmd_test(opts):
    root,book=load_book_obj(opts)
    cfg=book.cfg
    # library paths -> absolute (cwd join, no normalization)
    lib_dirs=[]
    for p in (opts.get("library_path") or []):
        lib_dirs.append(path_join(os.getcwd(),p) if not os.path.isabs(p) else p)
    from .book import run_preprocessors
    processed=run_preprocessors(book.book,cfg,"test")
    chapters=iter_chapters(processed)
    target_chapter=opts.get("chapter")
    to_test=[]
    for ch in chapters:
        if not ch.get("path"): continue
        if target_chapter is None or ch["name"]==target_chapter or ch.get("path")==target_chapter or ch.get("source_path")==target_chapter:
            # upstream matches name or path (path after preprocessors); source_path same normally. Avoid double-count path spelling variants: path check above may match source only when path equals too typically.
            if target_chapter is None or ch["name"]==target_chapter or ch.get("path")==target_chapter:
                to_test.append(ch)
    if target_chapter is not None and not to_test:
        raise MdError(f"Chapter not found: {target_chapter}")
    edition=cfg.rust.edition_str
    success=True
    # temp dir
    tmpbase=os.environ.get("TMPDIR") or tempfile.gettempdir()
    tmpdir=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mdbook-",dir=tmpbase)
    try:
        for ch in to_test:
            rel=ch["path"]
            log.info("mdbook_driver::mdbook",f'Testing chapter \'{ch["name"]}\': "{rel}"')
            out_path=path_join(tmpdir,rel)
            parent=os.path.dirname(out_path)
            if parent: os.makedirs(parent,exist_ok=True)
            with open(out_path,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(ch.get("content",""))
            args=["rustdoc",rel,"--test"]
            for d in lib_dirs: args+=["-L",d]
            args+=["--edition",edition]
            try:
                proc=subprocess.run(args,cwd=tmpdir,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
            except FileNotFoundError as e:
                raise MdError("failed to execute `rustdoc`",[os_error_str(e)])
            except OSError as e:
                raise MdError("failed to execute `rustdoc`",[os_error_str(e)])
            if proc.returncode!=0:
                success=False
                stdout=proc.stdout.decode('utf-8',errors='replace')
                stderr=proc.stderr.decode('utf-8',errors='replace')
                log.error("mdbook_driver::mdbook",f"rustdoc returned an error:\n\n--- stdout\n{stdout}\n\n--- stderr\n{stderr}")
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir,ignore_errors=True)
    if not success:
        raise MdError("One or more tests failed")
    return 0

def cmd_watch(opts):
    from .server import run_watch
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    # initial load (fatal errors)
    book=MDBook.load(root)
    dest=get_dest_dir(opts,root,book.cfg)
    book.dest_override=dest
    if opts.get("open"):
        build_book(book)
        rc=try_open_index(book,dest,"watch")
        if rc!=0: return rc
    run_watch(root,dest,opts.get("watcher") or "poll",opts.get("open"),initial_book=book)
    return 0

def cmd_serve(opts):
    from .server import run_watch, serve_forever, ServeState
    root=abs_path(opts.get("dir")) if opts.get("dir") else os.getcwd()
    book=MDBook.load(root)
    dest=get_dest_dir(opts,root,book.cfg)
    book.dest_override=dest
    book.live_reload_endpoint="__livereload"
    build_book(book)
    hostname=opts.get("hostname") or "localhost"; port_str=opts.get("port") or "3000"
    # parse port as Rust u16: optional leading '+', digits, range
    if not re.fullmatch(r'\+?\d+',port_str or ""):
        raise MdError("invalid port value")
    try: port=int(port_str)
    except Exception: raise MdError("invalid port value")
    if port>65535: raise MdError("invalid port value")
    # resolve address (first result)
    try:
        infos=socket.getaddrinfo(hostname,port,type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    except socket.gaierror as e:
        msg=e.strerror or str(e)
        raise MdError(f"failed to lookup address information: {msg}")
    if not infos:
        raise MdError("failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known")
    addr=infos[0]
    build_dir=book.build_dir_for("html")
    # fallback 404 file
    html_cfg=book.cfg.html_config()
    if html_cfg.input_404=="":
        fallback=None
    else:
        outname=(html_cfg.input_404.replace(".md",".html") if html_cfg.input_404 else "404.html")
        fallback=path_join(build_dir,outname)
    state=ServeState(build_dir,fallback)
    log.info("mdbook::cmd::serve",f"Serving on: http://{hostname}:{port_str}")
    if opts.get("open"):
        open_browser_path(f"http://{hostname}:{port_str}")
    stop=threading.Event()
    watch_thread=threading.Thread(target=_serve_watch_thread,args=(root,dest,opts.get("watcher") or "poll",state,book,stop),daemon=True)
    watch_thread.start()
    try:
        rc=serve_forever(state,hostname,port,hostname,port_str,addr)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        rc=0
    stop.set()
    return rc

def _serve_watch_thread(root,dest,watcher_kind,state,initial_book,stop):
    from .server import run_watch
    run_watch(root,dest,watcher_kind,False,live_reload="__livereload",on_rebuild=state.broadcast_reload,initial_book=initial_book,stop_event=stop)
